quickAnswer: Packaged snack manufacturers in Irinjalakuda must integrate statutory food safety compliance with intellectual property protection. Operating lawfully requires an active FSSAI State License or Registration via FoSCoS and adherence to FSS (Packaging and Labelling) Regulations. Protecting the brand name requires filing on Form TM-A under Class 29 (banana chips, tapioca chips, processed fruit snacks) and Class 30 (namkeen mixtures, baked savouries, confectionery). Securing your trademark before printing thousands of retail pouches prevents costly packaging recalls.

h2Sections.h2: Irinjalakuda's Famed Snack Heritage: Transitioning from Local to Packaged
content: Irinjalakuda, historically celebrated for the ancient Koodalmanikyam Temple and its cultural traditions, is equally famous across central Kerala for its traditional snack makers and confectioners. Renowned for crispy golden banana chips fried in pure coconut oil, authentic sharkkara upperi (jaggery-coated banana crisps), spicy mixture, and regional savouries, Irinjalakuda's snack enterprises have long supplied local bakeries and festive gatherings.

In recent years, many traditional snack producers have begun transitioning into modern packaged consumer goods, aiming for retail distribution across Kerala, national supermarkets, and Gulf export markets. However, commercial packaging brings strict regulatory responsibilities. Producers must simultaneously navigate mandatory FSSAI food safety licensing, precise packaging declarations, and statutory trademark registration to protect their commercial identity.

h2Sections.h2: The Mandatory Dual-Class Trademark Framework: Class 29 vs. Class 30
content: A critical legal hurdle in packaged snack branding is understanding the statutory boundary between Class 29 and Class 30 under the Nice Classification. Many producers mistakenly file under only one class, leaving half their product line defenseless.
The table below details how Irinjalakuda snack products are classified under Indian trademark law.

rows: Banana chips, fried tapioca chips, jackfruit crisps, roasted cashews, coconut oil snacks, processed potato chips.
Kerala mixture, murukku, pakavada, ribbon pakoda, sharkkara varatti, halwa, biscuits, confectionery.
Operating snack retail outlets, packaged food distribution agencies, e-commerce direct sales portals.
Operating on-site hot snack counters, sweet shops with dining seating, festive catering.

content: Under the Food Safety and Standards Act 2006, selling packaged snacks without an active FSSAI registration or license is a punishable offence carrying severe monetary penalties and confiscation of inventory.

1. FSSAI License Categories: Micro producers with annual turnover up to ₹12 Lakh require basic FSSAI Registration. Units with turnover between ₹12 Lakh and ₹20 Crore must obtain an FSSAI State License via the FoSCoS portal.

2. Mandatory Pouch Labeling: All retail pouches must prominently display: the 14-digit FSSAI License number, FSSAI logo, exact commercial brand name, complete ingredient list in descending order of weight, nutritional facts panel, vegetarian logo (green dot), Net Quantity, Date of Manufacture, Expiry / Best Before Date, Batch number, and complete manufacturer name and premises address.
3. Trademark Symbol Usage: Display the ™ symbol next to your brand name once Form TM-A is submitted, switching to the registered ® symbol only after the official certificate is issued.

callout.title: Never Print Packaging Before Trademark Clearance
callout.text: Never order tens of thousands of custom-printed laminate snack pouches before conducting an IP India trademark clearance search. If the Trade Marks Registry rejects your mark or an established brand sends a cease-and-desist notice, your entire packaging inventory must be destroyed.

h2Sections.h2: Actionable Launch Checklist for Snack Producers
content: Before shipping your packaged snacks to retail distributors, complete this verified compliance checklist:
checklist: Conduct phonetic trademark clearance search on IP India across Class 29 and Class 30
Submit Form TM-A to the Chennai Registry using an Udyam MSME certificate to secure the ₹4,500 fee rate
Apply for FSSAI State License or Registration via the FoSCoS online platform
Audit pouch artwork to ensure compliance with FSS (Packaging and Labelling) Regulations 2020
Obtain GST registration if annual business turnover exceeds statutory thresholds (₹40 Lakh for goods)
Maintain batch production registers, oil quality logs, and raw material sourcing invoices

h2Sections.h2: Frequently Asked Questions for Irinjalakuda Snack Makers
content:
Q: Can I register the name 'Irinjalakuda Banana Chips' as my exclusive trademark?
No. Geographic place names combined with generic product descriptions cannot be registered as private trademarks under Section 9(1)(b) of the Trade Marks Act 1999. You must adopt a distinctive, coined brand name (e.g., '[YourCoinedBrand] Irinjalakuda Banana Chips').

Q: Does an FSSAI license grant ownership over our snack brand name?
No. FSSAI is a food safety and public health regulatory authority. It does not grant intellectual property rights. Trademark ownership can only be secured through the Trade Marks Registry under the Trade Marks Act 1999.

Q: If our unit produces both banana chips and mixture, can we use one multi-class application?
Yes. You can file a consolidated multi-class Form TM-A covering both Class 29 and Class 30, paying the statutory fee for two classes (₹9,000 total for MSME/individual applicants).

faqs.question: Does an FSSAI license protect a snack brand name from being copied?
faqs.answer: No. An FSSAI license certifies food safety and hygiene compliance, but provides zero intellectual property protection. Only a registered trademark provides exclusive legal ownership over your brand name.

faqs.question: Which trademark class applies to Kerala banana chips?
faqs.answer: Banana chips, tapioca chips, and processed fruit snacks fall under Class 29, while flour-based snacks like mixture, murukku, and sweets fall under Class 30.

faqs.question: What is the penalty for selling packaged snacks without an FSSAI license?
faqs.answer: Operating a food business without a valid FSSAI license under Section 63 of the Food Safety and Standards Act 2006 is punishable with imprisonment up to 6 months and a fine up to ₹5 Lakh.
